The Assistant Secretary—Program Development and Budget will be responsible for reviewing and coordinating the activities of the several Eureaus involved. Specifically, he shall:
ORV use on all Interior lands and provide liaison on these matters with the Department of Agriculture, Department of Defense, Tennessee Valley Authority, and such other Federal land managing agencies as may authorize ORV use.
Provide technical assistance to all Interior Bureaus, other Federal agencies, the States and their local governments, and the private sector in coordinating, planning, and programming for the development of areas and facilities for the use of ORV.
3) Coordinate Departmental research and studies regarding the environmental impact of ORV.
Each Assistant Secretary with authorities and responsibilities for the administration of lands shall:
1) Review existing policies, rules, and regulations governing ORV use on lands under his jurisdiction to assure full compliance with the policy and intent of the Executive Order and Secretarial memorandum.
2) Designate all lands for ORV use as open (with controls) or closed. In order to establish appropriate levels of ORV use, restrictions or controls may be developed, where necessary, to protect unique natural features, special soil or vegetative conditions, wildlife and habitat areas, natural and historical areas, and other important factors.
3) Prepare for public information purposes a compilation and description of those lands and facilities available for ORV .use. For efficiency and economy in distribution, such publications can be developed for regional or local areas.
4) Recommend for adoption those regulations necessary to implement the following criteria and policies:
a) Definitions
(i) Off-Road Vehicle
An off-road vehicle is any motorized vehicle (including the standard automobile) which is used off established roadways and is designed for, or capable of, travel on or immediately over land, water, sand, snow, ice, marsh, swampland, or other
